cells.tense: You are moving with what you feel, and the ending ahead is being made by your own hand.
cells.act: dream it from what you have already lived
cells.ask: Think back to a chapter that closed and the next one that started anyway. What did you do back then that helped, even a little? Do that much again this week.
cells.core: The push toward what you want runs on what you feel, not on what looks right from outside. Where something is ending, you can hold both sides at once, the pull forward and the cut behind, and that isn't confusion. It's how you work. What you've already lived through is the material for what comes next. A chapter closed before this one, and the next one started, and you know what let that happen. Bring it into this ending. Something small and true, done once, is enough. You don't need the whole road lit. Enough light for the next step, none past it, is how this has gone before. The ending you're making is yours to make, and it doesn't ask you to know how it lands.
cells.sheetLine: What closed before lights what closes now.
cells.verb: Pushing steadily toward a destination that keeps changing shape
cells.place: Standing in a room stripped to what still matters

cells.tense: You will keep driving toward a destination that already arrived, and the stopping is what frightens you.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: Turn the pressure on something down a little, then leave it. Not a lurch to the other side, just enough that you can feel a difference. Then nothing more.
cells.core: Some momentum in you has passed the point where it helps. The ending is over and you keep the engine running, because stopping would mean it's real. That isn't weakness. It's forward motion that can't land. Underneath, the room feels like one more mile, one more push, one more maybe. Bring something adjacent in instead. Not the destination — one small turn of the pressure. Adjust it by a little and then stop. Not a swing to the opposite side. Just enough that the motion can breathe. You'll know in your body whether it landed, and either answer is fine. The next turn can wait until tomorrow.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you and not going through.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Name on paper what has finished, once, and leave the paper where you'll pass it. Don't add to it or reopen it.
cells.core: There's a place in your life where the feeling came before the motion did, and the motion hasn't come. You stand at the door, waiting for ready. When this works, the ending is allowed to be over and the next thing gets a cleared place to start from. You don't have to feel finished to be finished. That waiting is where the stuck sits — not the ending itself, but waiting for permission to have ended. Bring something plain to it. A sentence on paper. A drawer cleared. A number gone. The form doesn't matter, only that it's done once and not picked up again. Whatever it is, it says the line is drawn.

cells.tense: You are clearing the room and haven't noticed that your own hand did the clearing.
cells.act: stop holding up the false thing and watch it come down
cells.ask: Stop propping up a routine or a role you've kept steady out of habit. Let it lean unsupported and notice whether it stands or falls. Nothing more than watching.
cells.core: Something in this ending is being carried by you alone, and you'd say it was just how things go. The room stays upright because you keep it upright, and your name isn't on that work. Look at what's holding the roof. A routine, a role, an assumption about how this has to go — stop propping it and see whether it falls or stands. Either answer tells you something you didn't know. Not a decision, not a plan. Just your hands off it for a week. You'll have watched your own hand be the one that made the room look finished.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing is yours and you haven't signed it.
